text:
Brayden Point scored twice in the first 13 minutes, both snap shots set up by Nikita Kucherov, and Tampa Bay had a 2-0 lead before Detroit had a real look. Point went 79th overall in 2014 out of Moose Jaw, and on this night he looked like the first pick on his own team's sheet. Anthony Cirelli made it 3-0 in the second, and the Lightning held on for a 4-2 win after Ryan McDonagh scored at 19:59 of the third.

The numbers say the game was more of a fight than the final suggests. In expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, TBL won the first period 1.85 to 0.24. Detroit then took over: it out-chanced Tampa Bay 1.06 to 1.41 in the second and 1.83 to 0.75 in the third. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher scored to cut it to 3-2, and Michael Rasmussen had a 47% look in the third that Andrei Vasilevskiy turned away. Overall TBL held the edge in chances (4.00 expected goals to 3.12), and our simulation of every shot gives the Lightning a 63% chance of winning a replay, which we call deserved to win. That is a clear edge, not a lopsided one.

Vasilevskiy was the reason the lead survived. He saved 1.1 goals more than his 21 shots deserved, and without that the third period turns tense in a different way. Detroit used two goalies, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 12 of 13 after John Gibson allowed two on 13. The Lightning leave with the win and a night where their first period decided the game. Detroit leaves with a third-period push that came too late, and we'd watch whether it starts the next game that way.
